title: Blind-flight bench: radar altimeter + Copernicus GLO-30 TRN, six navigators on one harness
summary: Benchmark harness that reproduces the 2026 'Polyot vslepuyu' (Blind flight) hackathon case on four real GLO-30 windows (Khibiny mountains, Middle Urals, Yenisei taiga, the flat Moscow-region map area): 20 km simulated flights at a constant 1500 m baro level, a leading-edge radar altimeter with a 40 deg beam footprint, range noise, dropouts, outliers, baro bias and drift, map error and canopy, delivered as checksummed $GPGGA lines. Scores dead reckoning on the hints, our TERCOM baseline (core.tercom_fix from terrain-heightmap-pf) and our particle filter, each also against a precomputed beam-aware reference map, plus clean-room re-implementations (from README text only) of the GORIZONT multi-hypothesis tracker and the Gagarin MAD/NCC gated pipeline. Leaderboard of median/p95 error at 5/10/20 km, divergence rate, CPU and worst-step latency, and a one-impairment-at-a-time ablation.
verified: ran 2026-11-06 with CPython 3.13.15 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 / rasterio 1.5.2 on an Apple M2 Max: regions.py fetched the four GLO-30 windows over public HTTPS through terrain-heightmap-pf/fetch_dem.py; run_bench.py produced out/results.json and the leaderboard (80 flights x 10 navigators, 349 s wall) and --ablation produced out/ablation.md (144 flights x 6 navigators); two full runs gave identical error numbers for unchanged navigators. unittest: 10 passed in the venv; with plain python3 and no third-party packages 3 metric tests pass and 7 skip. Mutating error_at_distances (bisect_left => bisect_right) or the sign of the TERCOM correction makes a test fail. Flights, altimeter, baro error, map error and canopy are simulated with assumed parameters; the GORIZONT and Gagarin navigators are our re-implementations from their README text, not their code, and no team code was run.
